title: Constitutional Authority
description: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is an autonomous constitutional body established under Article 324. It is responsible for administering election processes for Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislatures, President, and Vice President.
details: ECI was established on 25 January 1950. It comprises the Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners. The CEC can only be removed by the President through a process similar to removing a Supreme Court judge. Current CEC: Gyanesh Kumar (since Feb 2025).

title: Model Code of Conduct
description: The MCC is a set of guidelines issued by ECI for political parties and candidates during elections. It becomes operative from the date of announcement of elections and remains in force till the date of counting.
details: MCC prohibits: use of government machinery for campaigning, communal appeals, bribery of voters, defacement of public property. Parties must remove campaign material within 48 hours of MCC activation. Violation can lead to withdrawal of candidature.

title: Electoral Roll Preparation
description: Every citizen aged 18+ on the qualifying date (1 Jan of the year) is eligible to register. NVSP (nvsp.in) is the online portal for registration. Special drives are conducted for new voters.
details: Approved voter IDs: 1) Aadhaar Card, 2) EPIC Card, 3) MNREGA Job Card, 4) Bank/Post Office Passbook with photo, 5) Health Insurance Smart Card, 6) Driving Licence, 7) PAN Card, 8) Indian Passport, 9) Smart Card issued by RGI, 10) Pension Document with photo, 11) Service Identity Card with photo (Govt employees), 12) Official identity document issued by MP/MLA/MLC. NRIs can register under Form 6A.

title: Nomination & Scrutiny
description: A candidate files nomination with Returning Officer. Deposit: ₹25,000 for LS (₹12,500 SC/ST). Nomination is scrutinised for eligibility. Candidate can withdraw within last date.
details: Eligibility: Indian citizen, 25+ years for LS (30+ for RS), not declared of unsound mind, not convicted with 2+ years sentence (unless stayed). Proposers needed: 1 registered voter from constituency. Candidature is forfeited if candidate gets less than 1/6th of votes polled.

title: Campaign Period
description: Campaign ends 48 hours before voting (silent period). Parties use rallies, door-to-door, digital campaigns, manifesto releases. Expenditure limits: ₹95 lakh per candidate for LS seats.
details: Section 126 RPA 1951 prohibits public meetings within 48 hours of polling. Exit polls can only be published after last phase of voting ends. Campaign finances tracked by expenditure observers. No paid news allowed. Social media campaigns must comply with ECI's IT guidelines.

title: Polling Day & EVM
description: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) are standalone devices not connected to any network. VVPAT (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail) shows a 7-second slip of your vote for verification.
details: EVM specs: max 2000 votes per BU (Ballot Unit), 64 candidates max. VVPAT slip visible for 7 seconds. Minimum 5 VVPAT machines verified per assembly segment. Polling hours: 7 AM – 6 PM (may vary). Voters must bring approved ID proof. Ink mark on left index finger.

title: Vote Counting
description: Counting happens at designated centres under strict security. Results are declared round by round. The candidate with most votes wins (FPTP — First Past The Post system).
details: India uses FPTP (plurality) system — no minimum percentage required to win. Counting observers from ECI are present. Re-counting can be requested. Results uploaded to ECI website in real-time. Postal ballots from service voters counted first. NOTA votes are counted but cannot win.

title: Anti-Defection Law
description: Added by 52nd Amendment (1985), the Tenth Schedule prevents elected members from defecting to other parties. Defecting MPs/MLAs lose their seat.
details: Disqualification occurs if: member voluntarily gives up party membership, votes contrary to party direction without prior permission. Exceptions: merger of 2/3rd members with another party. Decision lies with Speaker/Chairman — subject to judicial review. Notable cases: MP Himanta Biswa Sarma (2015), several in Maharashtra (2022).

title: Government Formation
description: After results, the President invites the leader of the majority party/alliance to form government. PM is sworn in by the President. Cabinet is formed within days.
details: Majority: 272+ seats in 543-seat Lok Sabha. If no single party has majority, coalition negotiations happen. President's Rule (Article 356) if no government can be formed. PM leads Council of Ministers — accountable to Lok Sabha. Government can be brought down by a no-confidence motion (simple majority).

title: Legal Framework
description: India's election law is governed by multiple statutes ensuring free, fair, and transparent elections.
details: Key laws: 1) Representation of the People Act 1950 — electoral rolls, qualifications. 2) Representation of the People Act 1951 — conduct of elections, corrupt practices, disputes. 3) Delimitation Act 2002 — boundary drawing. 4) Election Commission Act 1991 — ECI structure. 5) Constitution Article 243ZA — local body elections. 6) NOTA — Supreme Court order 2013.
